title: In 2022, a Volcano Fired 2,600 Lightning Bolts a Minute

scenes.text: In 2022, a volcano fired 2,600 lightning bolts a minute.
Hunga Tonga erupted under the Pacific and threw ash 36 miles up. Higher than any plane flies.
The plume made its own storm. 192,000 flashes in eleven hours. The most intense lightning ever recorded.
Some bolts struck 19 miles above sea level. The rings of lightning stretched 155 miles across.
Ash and ice smash together in the plume and build up charge. A thunderstorm on steroids.
2,600 bolts a minute. From one volcano.

description:
The January 2022 eruption of Hunga Tonga in the Pacific produced the most intense lightning ever recorded: a peak of over 2,600 flashes per minute and about 192,000 flashes over eleven hours.
The ash plume reached at least 58 kilometres (36 miles) high, lightning fired 20 to 30 kilometres above sea level, and the rings of lightning grew to 250 kilometres across.
Would you rather see a volcano or a lightning storm up close? Comment below.
first_comment: The same eruption sent a pressure wave around the planet several times and was heard in Alaska, 6,000 miles away. What is the loudest thing you have ever heard?
